_meta.indication: Adjunct to lipid-lowering medications and diet to reduce LDL-C, apolipoprotein B (apo B), total cholesterol (TC), and non-HDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: ISIS 301012-CS5 (also referred to as ISIS-CS5), the single phase 3 trial in patients with HoFH
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents for ISIS 301012-CS5
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study with a 26-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) on stable lipid-lowering therapy; baseline LDL-C approximately 420 mg/dl
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was the percent change in LDL-C
pivotal_trials.result: Mean percent change in LDL-C was -24.7% with mipomersen vs -3.3% with placebo (p<0.001); treatment difference from placebo was -21.4%

key_safety: Most common AEs were injection-site reactions (84% mipomersen vs 33% placebo) and flu-like symptoms (30% vs 16%). Hepatotoxicity: in the HoFH trial 12% (4/34) of mipomersen patients had ALT ≥3xULN vs 0% placebo; median increase in hepatic fat fraction 9.6% vs 0.02% placebo. Mipomersen is highly immunogenic (ADA 33% at Week 50).
target_moa: First-in-class antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) inhibitor of apolipoprotein B-100 (apo B), the principal apolipoprotein of LDL, inhibiting apo B-100 synthesis

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF HEPATOTOXICITY — KYNAMRO can cause elevations in transaminases; 4 (12%) of 34 mipomersen patients vs 0% of 17 placebo had ALT ≥3xULN, and it increases hepatic fat (median absolute increase 10% after 26 weeks in HeFH/hyperlipidemia trials), a risk factor for advanced liver disease including steatohepatitis and cirrhosis.

rems.type: Because of the risk of hepatotoxicity, KYNAMRO is available only through a restricted program under a REMS called the KYNAMRO REMS, with elements to assure safe use to mitigate the risk of elevated liver transaminases and hepatic steatosis.

advisory_committee.vote: The advisory committee met on 18 October 2012; when asked if the efficacy and safety data supported marketing for treatment of HoFH, the committee voted 9 "yes" and 6 "no".

orphan_indication.text: Treatment of homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) is an orphan indication.

citations.quote: This memo summarizes the basis of the regulatory action for this new drug application seeking an orphan indication of the treatment of homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH).
Because the treatment of HoFH is an orphan indication, the company was not required to address the study of mipomersen in the pediatric population.

summary.text: Kynamro (mipomersen), a first-in-class antisense oligonucleotide, was reviewed as a standard (Type 1 NME 505(b)(1)) application for the orphan indication of HoFH and approved January 29, 2013 following a 9-to-6 advisory committee vote, with a REMS and four postmarketing requirements.
